purpose: Illustrated Ink replay segmentation and image-prompt controls for the last downstream clearance interval during the Shortened Watch Failure.

visual_scene_plan.purpose: Click-through anchors for ordinary channel work, the four-record comparison, visible process divergence, competing warnings, accepted release, rescue, and four families of historical consequence.
visual_scene_plan.segmentation_rule: Use separate visual_scene_id anchors for the clearance-house establishing frame, record closeup, preparation choice, routine fold, first process sign, warning choice, signal fold, accepted-release beat, first surge response, irreversible threshold, and each ending family. The lifted grit and the first water around the bend each receive a discrete replay beat.
visual_scene_plan.prompting_rule: Each base image prompt restates drawable geometry, materials, light, bodies, interfaces, and key objects for a general image model. Continuity notes stay in tooling fields; prompt assembly uses only visible character refs and triggered visible deltas.
visual_scene_plan.global_style_cue: Style: hand-painted high-fantasy interactive-fiction illustration, gouache and ink on textured paper, sharp readable silhouettes, permanent-twilight blue and rain-muted stone, oxidized bronze and old dark metal, warm ochre work lamps, restrained historical realism, tactile labor detail, abstract unlettered record marks, humane faces under practical pressure.
visual_scene_plan.prompt_assembly_rule: Assemble every render prompt from the global_style_cue, one scene base_image_prompt, visual refs only for named characters or groups visible in that frame, and triggered state_image_modifiers or global_branch_image_modifiers. Continuity notes and off-frame character refs stay outside the prompt.

scene_set_guidance.scope_reason: The fixture returns to one small multi-level workface from several angles and branches change routes, props, water, and character positions. The structured scene_set below is the durable draft geometry authority for prose and prompt review.
scene_set_guidance.future_scene_set_need: Before high-consistency website rendering, lower this map into a plan view or simple 3D blockout with the record bay, upstream shutter, bell frame, covered stair, landing, rescue shelf, channel floor, side hollow, outflow bend, and distant gatehouse sightline.

scenes.base_image_prompt: Wide exterior-interior cutaway view of a compact public-works clearance house built into the stone bank above a broad masonry outflow channel under permanent twilight. The house has thick rain-dark walls, an upstream-facing pale signal shutter, a bronze bell frame beside a lower door, a waist-high record table under ochre oil lamps, and a covered stone stair descending to a wet channel floor. A short landing leads to a raised rescue shelf above the water line. Far upstream, an old dark metal release throat is set inside newer stone and a small gatehouse stands in the shutter sightline. Down-channel, work yards and low occupied roofs follow the bend. Isca Rel stands by the bell frame; Dema Tern is at the record table; Anet Vos directs a mud-streaked crew below; Pel Orra braces a timber frame on the channel floor.

visible_characters.default_stance: beside the bell frame, counting people below
at the record table with a rolled work board
on the lower landing directing the crew
on the channel floor at a timber brace
working at braces along the channel floor

visual_continuity_notes: The clearance house occupies the upper bank at one channel bend. Interior record bay, bell frame, upstream shutter, landing, rescue shelf, stair, side hollow, and channel floor retain fixed adjacency.
The distant gatehouse is visible only through the upstream shutter sightline; speech cannot cross the distance.

scenes.base_image_prompt: Close overhead evidence view on a scarred waist-high wooden table inside a stone clearance house. Four distinct work records sit beneath one painted heading board: a protected old source copy in a dark metal-edged sleeve, a small signed conversion slip, a larger manager-approved work board, and a narrow tally of warnings carried down-channel. Their marks are abstract and unlettered but visibly different in age, material, handwriting, and seals. Isca Rel's callused finger points between them while Dema Tern's clean dark cuff and seal hand rest beside the conversion slip. An ochre lamp warms the records; blue twilight and spray enter through the pale upstream signal shutter behind them.

hand beside the signed conversion

visual_character_refs.purpose: Stable named-character and group visual identities for prompt assembly. Include only refs for bodies visible in a scene.

characters.isca_rel: Isca Rel: human clearance keeper in her late thirties or forties, medium-brown skin, strong narrow face, close dark curls threaded with gray, dark eyes, copper-brown waxed work coat over layered slate-blue wool, broad blue warning sash, fingerless leather gloves, high strapped boots, compact practical silhouette, body language that checks exits and counts people before addressing rank.
characters.anet_vos: Anet Vos: human channel foreperson in her forties or fifties, deep brown skin, broad shoulders, shaved head, heavy brows, sleeveless dark waxed-leather work vest over rolled ochre linen, belt of wooden wedges and chalk, silt-black hands and boots, stable low stance, gestures with whole hand toward routes and named workers.
characters.pel_orra: Pel Orra: young human brace worker in late teens or early twenties, pale freckled skin, thick black curls tied with a red cord, olive wool tunic under a short gray oilskin cape, wrapped forearms, mud-dark trousers and boots, lean unfinished strength, quick grin that vanishes under danger, often carrying a basket of iron pins or gripping rescue line.
characters.dema_tern: Dema Tern: human conversion clerk in his thirties or forties, warm brown skin, long black braid bound in bronze rings, fine angular face, cream-gray layered clerk coat with dark clean cuffs, narrow seal belt, lacquered document tube, upright economical posture, hands kept close to the signed conversion and approved board until the flood forces physical work.

groups.channel_crew: Channel crew: six human public-works laborers of varied ages, skin tones, builds, and genders, wearing layered wool and linen under short waxed capes, wrapped forearms, rope belts, high leather boots, silt-streaked faces, carrying timber braces, mallets, wedges, iron shoes, pin baskets, and hemp lines; bodies crouched low for leverage or staggered in an extraction line.
groups.lower_yard_residents: Lower-yard residents and workers: mixed-age human figures in rain capes, work aprons, layered tunics, head wraps, and high boots, moving among drying racks, carts, baskets, low stone-and-timber roofs, and the covered stair; adults carry tools, goods, or small children while others guide carts toward higher routes.

review_notes: No images were generated. This visual plan and the BFL prompt batch are the complete visual deliverables for the pass.

The fixture is multi-angle and branch-persistent. Its structured scene_set is sufficient for draft staging and prompt review; high-consistency website rendering still requires a plan-view or 3D blockout derived from it.
Every base prompt is self-contained and uses affirmative visible geometry, materials, bodies, lighting, objects, and positions.
The old release throat is presented as material infrastructure. The fixture does not invent visible magic, a universal machine interface, or readable fictional text.
